groups.problem: update/destroy look up the host with where(id:).first and never check for nil, so an unknown id raises NoMethodError (500) instead of returning 404.
groups.rationale: All three report the same missing nil guard in EmbeddableHostsController update/destroy and suggest the same fix.

groups.problem: The before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! without a nil guard, so a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation.
groups.rationale: All three point at the same callback lines and describe the same nil crash.

groups.problem: The migration inserts the raw host values, scheme and path included, without normalizing them, so migrated rows never match record_for_host/host_allowed?.
groups.rationale: All three describe the same missing normalization in the migration INSERT and propose stripping the scheme and path.

groups.problem: The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped, so each file defines the other file's fabricators.
groups.rationale: One swap affects both files, and moving the contents back fixes it for both.

groups.problem: The new admin controller specs only check inheritance from AdminController and do not test any controller actions.
groups.rationale: The same weak test pattern appears in the two new controller spec files, and both need the same kind of request specs.

problems: update/destroy do not guard against a nil host when the id is unknown, which causes NoMethodError and a 500.
A missing params[:embeddable_host] causes NoMethodError, so strong params or validation are needed.
uncoveredProblems: A missing params[:embeddable_host] causes NoMethodError in save_host.

problems: The migration interpolates the host directly into SQL, which allows SQL injection or a syntax error.
The migration skips host normalization, so lookups never match.
uncoveredProblems: The migration interpolates the raw host into SQL without escaping, which allows SQL injection or a syntax error.

problems: The migration dereferences [0] of an execute result without checking whether it is empty, which causes NoMethodError.
The INSERT interpolates the host without quoting, so a single quote breaks the SQL.
uncoveredProblems: The migration dereferences [0] of possibly empty query results, so a missing row raises NoMethodError.
The migration INSERT interpolates the raw host without quoting or escaping, which can break the SQL.
